svg.title: New Thread runtime and root flyout layout variants
svg.desc: Three exploratory Beryl flyout layouts: a two-pane browser, an expandable runtime tree, and a search-first recent-target picker, plus the common zero-runtime state.
svg.text: Three deliberately different information architectures, shown in the split-button’s real shell context.
Choose where the new thread runs
Pick a runtime, then one of its roots. Nothing changes until you confirm.
An eligible empty thread may be reused here.
Esc cancels · Enter confirms the selected root
Runtime context stays fixed while roots are scanned; add actions live beside
the collection they change. Explicit confirmation prevents an exploratory click
from creating or switching a thread.
Widest flyout. Both lists should use stable row ids and bounded rendering if
Expand a runtime, then activate a root to create immediately.
Root rows are commands · Esc closes without creating
Narrow, familiar, and visually honest about the runtime/root hierarchy. Add-root
stays inside its runtime; Add runtime remains global.
More vertical travel, and direct root activation is fast but less forgiving. With
many expanded runtimes this becomes a virtualized tree rather than a simple menu.
Optimized for returning to a small set of roots across several runtimes.
Search path, root name, or runtime…
Arrow keys select · Enter confirms · Esc cancels
The common path is nearly flat: recent targets first, search always focused,
runtime management still visible below. Friendly to keyboard-heavy use.
The hierarchy is less obvious, and ranking becomes product behavior. It needs
clear stable ordering so the flyout never feels like a moving target.
Zero runtimes uses the same split button
Primary stays disabled; the secondary segment draws attention.
Adding the first runtime provisions Home and the first thread.
Add Windows or a WSL runtime to begin.
Its user-home root is created automatically.
The runtime picker/probe may continue from this command.
One successful setup action produces a usable window context.
